definitions.explanation: A job title, official position, or credential attached to a person's name. Used on business cards, in introductions, and when describing someone's professional status. Can also refer more broadly to any label or qualification that defines someone's social standing.

examples.japanese: {名刺|めいし}に{肩書|かたが}きを{入|い}れる。
examples.english: Put a title on a business card.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{立派|りっぱ}な{肩書|かたが}きを{持|も}っている。
{肩書|かたが}きに{頼|たよ}らず{実力|じつりょく}で{勝負|しょうぶ}したい。
examples.english: I want to compete on ability, not rely on titles.

notes:
USAGE NOTE:
Often used in discussions about Japanese business culture, where titles carry significant weight. The expression {肩書|かたが}きだけの refers to someone who has a title in name only, without real authority or ability.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {肩書|かたが}きを{持|も}つ (have a title)
- {肩書|かたが}きに{頼|たよ}る (rely on one's title)
- {肩書|かたが}きだけの (title-only, nominal)
- {肩書|かたが}きがない (have no title/credentials)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {役職|やくしょく}: position, post (specifically within an organization hierarchy)
- {称号|しょうごう}: honorary title or degree (more formal/academic)
